paragraphs.title: The Shortness of Human Life and the Plea for Rest

answers: Long and peaceful
Of few days and full of trouble
Unchanging and without sorrow
easy.explanation: Job says that man is "of few days, and full of trouble."
easy.q: How does Job describe the life of man?

answers: A flower and a shadow
A sea and a river
A mountain and a tree
easy.explanation: Man comes forth like a flower and flees like a shadow.
easy.q: What is man compared to in the opening verses?

answers: Give him endless life
Turn him into a tree
Turn from him and let him rest
easy.explanation: Job asks God to turn from him so that he may rest until his appointed time is complete.
easy.q: What does Job ask God to do?

answers: Because man is limited and short-lived
Because man is stronger than God
Because man never dies
medium.explanation: Job has described man as weak, troubled, and short-lived, so he wonders why such a creature is brought into judgment.
medium.q: Why does Job question why God brings man into judgment?

answers: His name
His fixed limits or appointed time
His strength
medium.explanation: The verse speaks of limits placed upon the length and course of human life.
medium.q: In the phrase "thou hast appointed his bounds that he cannot pass," what does "bounds" mean?

answers: Man is renewed, then asks for judgment
Man is described as short-lived, the question of judgment is raised, and a plea for rest follows
Man becomes a tree and then dries up
medium.explanation: Job first describes human weakness and brevity, then questions judgment and asks for relief.
medium.q: What is the main sequence of thought in verses 1–6?

answers: That it is stable and permanent
That it is passing and uncertain
That it is stronger than nature
challenge.explanation: A flower is cut down and a shadow flees, emphasizing the temporary nature of human life.
challenge.q: What does the comparison with a flower and a shadow emphasize about human life?

answers: It emphasizes human limitation and lack of perfection
It proves that man does not need rest
It describes the renewal of a tree
challenge.explanation: The statement presents human beings as unable to produce purity from impurity, highlighting their limitation.
challenge.q: How does the statement "Who can bring a clean thing out of an unclean? not one" relate to Job's request?

answers: Because man's days are limited, Job asks to pass them in peace
Because man's days are endless, Job asks them to stop
Because man is renewed, Job asks to become a tree
challenge.explanation: Since human life has appointed limits, Job asks to be left alone until he completes his allotted days.
challenge.q: What connection is made between appointed days and Job's request for rest?

paragraphs.title: The Tree's Hope Compared with Human Finality

answers: It may sprout again
It disappears immediately without change
It becomes a man
easy.explanation: Job says that a cut tree may sprout again and send out a tender branch.
easy.q: What may happen to a tree after it is cut down?

answers: He dies, wastes away, and gives up the ghost
He blossoms after receiving a little water
He always returns to life
easy.explanation: Unlike the tree, man dies, wastes away, and gives up the ghost.
easy.q: What happens to man according to these verses?

answers: A falling mountain
Waters failing from the sea and a drying flood
A flower opening
easy.explanation: Job describes waters failing from the sea and a flood decaying and drying up.
easy.q: What does Job compare the finality of man to?

answers: Because it can renew itself after being cut down
Because it does not need water
Because man cannot die
medium.explanation: The tree may sprout again and bud through the scent of water.
medium.q: Why does the tree have greater hope than man in Job's description?

answers: Its upper branches
The main stem or base of the tree
The water around it
medium.explanation: The stock is the main body or base of the tree.
medium.q: What does "stock" mean in the phrase "the stock thereof die in the ground"?

answers: The tree is renewed, while man dies and disappears
Both are renewed in the same way
Man is renewed, while the tree immediately dries up
medium.explanation: The passage sets the tree's possibility of renewal against man's death and apparent finality.
medium.q: How does the contrast between the tree and man develop?

answers: That death is reversible
That death is final and irreversible
That man can restore the waters
challenge.explanation: The disappearing waters illustrate the loss and finality associated with man's death.
challenge.q: What does the comparison with waters failing and a flood drying up teach about man's death?

answers: It can bud through the scent of water
It lies down and does not rise
It loses all its roots
challenge.explanation: Job says, "through the scent of water it will bud, and bring forth boughs like a plant."
challenge.q: Which detail especially emphasizes the tree's ability to renew itself?

answers: Nature and man have equal power to renew themselves
Man is more passing and final than the tree
Man can grow again after death
challenge.explanation: The tree may sprout again, but man dies, wastes away, and does not rise in this description.
challenge.q: What central idea emerges from the comparison between the tree and man?

paragraphs.title: A Plea for Shelter in Sheol and Hope for an Answer

answers: In a garden
In the grave
On a mountain
easy.explanation: Job says, "Oh that thou wouldest hide me in the grave."
easy.q: Where does Job wish to be hidden?

answers: From God's wrath
From the tree
From the river
easy.explanation: He asks to be kept secret until God's wrath has passed.
easy.q: From what does Job want to be hidden?

answers: Forget him
Answer him
Send him to the mountain
easy.explanation: Job says, "Thou shalt call, and I will answer thee."
easy.q: What does Job ask God to do when He calls him?

answers: That it will have a set limit
That it will continue forever
That it will become a flower
medium.explanation: Job asks God to appoint him a set time and remember him, suggesting a limit to his suffering.
medium.q: What does Job hope will happen to his appointed time of suffering?

answers: Hide and preserve me from sight
Raise me from the dust
Send me to my children
medium.explanation: Job asks to be hidden in the grave until God's wrath has passed.
medium.q: What does "keep me secret" mean in the context of Job's request?

answers: To be hidden in the grave, to wait, and then to answer God's call
To be built, to blossom, and then to disappear
To be judged, to win, and then to forget God
medium.explanation: Job asks for shelter, waits for an appointed time, and hopes to answer when God calls.
medium.q: What is the main sequence in Job's request?

answers: Job asks to be hidden, but also hopes that God will remember and call him
Job wants to disappear and no longer have any connection with God
Job asks to become a tree and blossom again

challenge.q: How do the verses express both a plea for shelter and a hope for the future?

answers: That he is completely certain about life after death
That he is wrestling with the possibility of life after death
That he denies the reality of death
challenge.explanation: The question expresses uncertainty and longing as Job considers whether a dead man can live again.
challenge.q: What does the question "If a man die, shall he live again?" reveal about Job's condition?

answers: That they be preserved forever
That they not be remembered forever
That they be turned into righteousness
challenge.explanation: Job asks whether God is watching over his sin and describes his iniquity as sealed up, reflecting his concern about guilt being remembered.
challenge.q: What does Job ask concerning his sin and iniquity?

paragraphs.title: Human Erosion, Lost Hope, and Departure from the World

answers: They fall, are removed, and are worn away
They are immediately renewed
They become trees
easy.explanation: Job describes a mountain falling, a rock being removed, and stones being worn by water.
easy.q: What happens to mountains and rocks in these verses?

answers: What happens to his sons
Where the river is
How a tree grows
easy.explanation: The passage says that his sons may be honored or brought low, but he does not know or perceive it.
easy.q: What does a man not know after his death?

answers: Joy in body and soul
Pain in his flesh and mourning in his soul
Hope of renewal
easy.explanation: The final verse says, "his flesh upon him shall have pain, and his soul within him shall mourn."
easy.q: What remains with man at the end of the description?

answers: If even mountains and rocks wear away, man is certainly not everlasting
If mountains wear away, man becomes stronger
If stones wear away, man can renew himself
medium.explanation: The erosion of seemingly strong things in nature supports Job's portrayal of human weakness and mortality.
medium.q: How does the wearing away of mountains lead to a conclusion about man?

answers: Plants and growth arising from the ground
The deepest waters of a river
The peak of a mountain
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to things that grow from the earth and are washed away by the waters.
medium.q: What does "the things which grow out of the dust of the earth" refer to?

answers: He continues to know everything about his sons
He no longer knows or perceives what happens to his sons
He becomes young again
medium.explanation: Job says that a man does not know when his sons are honored or brought low.
medium.q: What is the result of man's aging and death according to these verses?

answers: Human hope is removed in view of mortality and decay
God promises man everlasting life
Man receives power to renew himself like a tree
challenge.explanation: The erosion of nature and the passing of man are presented as destroying human hope.
challenge.q: What does the statement "thou destroyest the hope of man" mean in the context of the chapter?

answers: Physical pain and sorrow of soul are presented together as man's final condition
Physical pain removes all inward sorrow
Sorrow of soul causes the body to be renewed
challenge.explanation: The verse joins pain in the flesh with mourning in the soul.
challenge.q: What relationship does the final verse create between bodily pain and inward mourning?

answers: Man continues to follow his sons after death
Man passes away, no longer knows about his sons, and is left with pain
Man returns to nature and grows again like a tree
challenge.explanation: Job describes man as passing away, losing awareness of his sons, and ending in bodily pain and inward mourning.
challenge.q: How is departure from the world expressed in the closing verses?
